question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $P$ above. Find the matrix of the quadratic form ${x}^{T}\,Ax$ in the basis that consists of the columns of $P.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $x=[{x}_{1},{x}_{2}]^{T}$ is a vector given by its coordinates in the standard basis and $y=[{y}_{1},{y}_{2}]^{T}$ is the same vector but given in the coordinates relative to the basis that consists of the columns of $P,$ then 

$$
x=Py.
$$

As a result, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ax & =(Py)^{T}\,A\,(Py) \\  & =({y}^{T}{P}^{T})\,A\,(Py) \\  & ={y}^{T}({P}^{T}\,AP)\,y,\end{aligned}
$$

which means that the matrix of our form in the new basis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{T}\,AP & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}18 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
